title: Adjacent Increasing Subarrays Detection II
summary: Given an array of integers, determine the largest k for which two adjacent subarrays of length k each are strictly increasing.
statement: Given an array of integers, determine the largest k for which two adjacent subarrays of length k each are strictly increasing. Both subarrays must start at indices a and a+k, respectively, where a < a+k. Return the maximum k.
constraints: Find two adjacent length-k subarrays such that both are strictly increasing.
Return the largest possible positive k.
hints: A valid pair either splits one increasing run or lies across the boundary of two consecutive runs.
At each run end, compare half its length with the smaller of this and the previous run length.
Scan maximal increasing runs and update max(current//2, min(previous,current)).
Those are the only two ways adjacent increasing blocks can sit inside the maximal-run partition.
editorial: Those are the only two ways adjacent increasing blocks can sit inside the maximal-run partition.

tests.explanation: Increasing runs of lengths five and three meet at the split, supporting adjacent length-three subarrays.
The first run can split into two length-two pieces, and no construction supports three.
